text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A ministerial meeting chaired by Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri discussed the draft investment law. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif said the main points of the law were: no nationalisation or confiscation of investments, no sequestration except by court ruling, no arbitrary cancellation of approvals, no adminstrative interference in pricing.
- The site has been dug for the main power station for lifting water at the pumping station for the New Valley project.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat discussed issues related to the interim period agreement between Israel and the Palestinians and preparations for the final status negotiations.

- The Public Monies prosecution department is investigating financial irregularities amounting to 30 million pounds ($8.8 million) in the mainly public-sector companies Stia/Nasr Woolen and Selected Textiles NWEP.CA, Vestia Ready-Made Garments and Misr El-Amria Spinning and Weaving. The chairman of Misr El-Amria, Ahmed Abu El-Wafa, has been banned from travelling abroad.
- No nationalisation or confiscation of investments.
- Health Minister Ismail Sallam performed two open heart operations in an Alexandria hospital yesterday.
- Saeb Erekat said the proposal on further stages of Israeli redeployment was born in Amr Moussa's office.
- Local Government Minister Mahmoud Sherif said the New Valley project will provide for seven million people, reducing the demographic pressure in the old valley.
- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi said Egypt would not let any other state interfere in its security affairs, in reference to the case of the letter bombs sent to the newspaper al-Hayat.
- The government has allocated two billion pounds to buy this year's cotton crop at 500 pounds a qantar (10 pounds a kg or about 134 centilibres), Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali announced.
- 300 workers in the industrial area of Sixth of October City had food poisoning from meat and rice they ate.
